title: Human-only approvals: refuse agent paths by entry point, grade proof by auth method
summary: How Kyberion keeps agents from settling human-only approvals, and the pitfalls hit while tightening it (HA-01..03).
hint_triggers:
Lessons from the first human-approval trust PR (MSN-APPROVAL-TRUST-20261010):

1. Refuse at every agent-facing entry point, not only the obvious ones. MCP approval.decide and the actuator decide op were covered by the plan; the terminal command run inside an agent session was not, and the reviewer found it still recorded a human, authenticated decision. Enumerate entry points (MCP, actuator, CLI, HTTP routes, scripts) when adding a refusal and test each.
2. Refuse rejects too. The first decision settles a record, so an agent reject blocks the real human approval.
3. Environment markers are advisory. detectAgentExecutionContext() unifies detection, but any in-process caller can still pass decidedByType/authMethod to decideApprovalRequest, and an agent can unset KYBERION_APPROVAL_ASSURANCE. Treat env-based checks as one layer; store-level refusal and policy-sourced modes are the durable fix.
4. Grade proof, do not trust a boolean. Map each authMethod to an assurance level (A0-A3), stamp min_assurance on creation (requesters may raise it, never lower it), and make the validator an allow-list so an unknown method is rejected.
5. Roll out with warn, but make warn loud: record the shortfall on the record and event log, audit it, and alert the operator with a next step, deduplicated by correlation_id. Do not enable enforce until every legitimate human path reaches the required level.
6. Re-checks of decided records must not re-grade assurance (phase recheck), or old decisions become unusable retroactively.
7. The type-ratchet max-lines baseline is the largest source file; growing that file fails the gate. Move cohesive helpers or types into sibling modules (re-export for compatibility) instead of raising the baseline.
